newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran president hopes for better ties with Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Iran president hopes for better ties with Saudi.

text.p: Iran's new President Mohammad Khatami has told Saudi Arabia's King Fahd that he hoped for a new chapter in relations between the two powerful and oil-rich Gulf states, Saudi state-run television said on Sunday.
It said Khatami sent the Saudi monarch a cable in which he expressed hope for "the opening of a new page in relations between the two brotherly countries to serve mutual interests."
The cable thanked King Fahd for his congratulatory message to Khatami following his victory in Iranian presidential elections last month, the television said.

Relations between Saudi Arabia and Iran have often been tense since Iran's 1979 Islamic revolution, mainly over the presence of Western forces in the Gulf, the annual Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca, Iran's armament programme and charges that Iran meddles in the internal affairs of its neighbours.
Iran, which denies the charges, and American allegations that it backs international terrorism, is trying to improve ties with Gulf Arab states.
Khatami, a moderate former culture minister, was elected president last month in an upset victory over Iran's conservative establishment.
King Fahd at the time expressed a desire for stronger relations with Iran in his message to Khatami.
Khatami will take over in August from President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
